explanations.2001-portuguese-local-elections--2002-po: Nothing obliged Guterres to resign: he had a legislature running to 2003 and the local result changed no seat in the Assembly. He resigned on the night, in his own phrase to avoid the country falling into a political swamp, and the president dissolved the Assembly in December for an election in March. The election of 2002 exists because of a ballot that was not about it, and the atlas keeps the edge as `caused` because the chain has no other link in it: local defeat, resignation, dissolution, early election, all inside three months.
explanations.2002-portuguese-legislative-election--20: The legislature this election returned should have run to 2006 and ran to 2005, and the reason is inside it. Durão Barroso left the government he led for the European Commission in July 2004; Santana Lopes took over without going back to the country; and in November President Sampaio dismissed the government — using, for the only time in the democratic period, the power to dissolve against a majority that still had one. The early election of February 2005 is the direct consequence of a prime minister leaving mid-term, and that is what the edge argues.
explanations.2005-portuguese-legislative-election--20: Holding the referendum again was a Socialist commitment in the 2005 campaign, made in as many words, and the absolute majority is what made it a decision rather than a negotiation: the Assembly approved the question, the president called it and the ballot was held on 11 February 2007. The atlas argues the direct line because there is no other: the question had been settled in the negative in 1998, no party had put it back since, and the government elected in 2005 put it back because it had said it would.
explanations.2009-portuguese-legislative-election--tr: The request of April 2011 was made by a government that had resigned, to a parliament that had refused its fourth austerity package, in a market that had stopped lending to it. The election of 2009 is where the arithmetic comes from: a Socialist government forty-nine seats short of a majority, dependent on opponents who had every reason to withhold the votes and then to force an election. The edge is `precondition-of` rather than `caused` because the debt, the deficit and the sovereign crisis in the euro area would have been there whatever the Assembly looked like — what this election settled was that there would be no majority to meet them with.
explanations.2011-portuguese-legislative-election--20: Sócrates resigned the leadership on the night of the defeat, as he had resigned the government in March, and the party had to elect a successor within weeks. The ballot of 22 and 23 July exists for that reason and no other. The atlas keeps a party’s internal election as an event where something follows from it, and what follows from this one is the leadership that the primary of 2014 was called to end.
explanations.2011-portuguese-legislative-election--tr: A three-year adjustment programme has to be carried by a government that survives it, and Portugal's was: the coalition elected in June 2011 was still in office in May 2014 and it left the programme without the precautionary credit line, which was its own decision and not the lenders'. The atlas argues the political condition rather than the economics. The memorandum was signed by a caretaker government of a party that then lost; what this election supplied was a majority that had campaigned on carrying it out and had four years to do so.
explanations.2011-portuguese-socialist-party-leadersh: The primary of 2014 was a challenge to a sitting leader, and this is the ballot that made him one. Seguro had been elected in 2011 without a contest of this kind and had never been the party's candidate for prime minister; the open primary was the instrument found to settle both questions at once, and it could only have been aimed at the incumbency this election created. The edge is `precondition-of` rather than `caused`: what 2011 produced was the position that was challenged, not the challenge.
explanations.2014-portuguese-socialist-party-prime-mi: The arithmetic of October 2015 was there whoever led the Socialists: the PS, the Bloco, the PCP and the Greens held a majority of the seats between them. What was not there in any previous parliament was a Socialist leader willing to govern on written agreements with the two parties to his left, and to argue in public that the largest list does not automatically govern. Costa had said so during the primary and won it saying so. The edge argues the disposition and not the numbers, which is why it is `enabled` and why the atlas keeps the primary as an event at all.
explanations.2022-portuguese-social-democratic-party-: The ballot of 27 November was brought forward by a week for a reason: the president had dissolved the Assembly on 5 November and the party needed a candidate for prime minister before the campaign. That is what this election chose — not only a leader for the next two years but the name at the head of the largest opposition list on 30 January. The edge is `precondition-of` because the legislative election was already called when this one was held: what the party settled was who would fight it, not that it would happen.

The government of April 2024 is a Democratic Alliance government, and the alliance with the CDS was Montenegro's own reconstruction of a formula last used in 1980. He could make it because this ballot had given him the party two years earlier, with a mandate that included going back to a coalition his predecessor had refused. The edge is `precondition-of`: what put him in the prime minister's office was the election of March 2024, and what put him at the head of the list that won it was this.
explanations.2023-madeiran-regional-election--2024-ma: The snap election of May 2024 was caused by a corruption investigation and a resignation, not by the ballot of September 2023. What the 2023 ballot fixed was when it could happen: the constitution forbids the president from dissolving a legislative assembly within six months of its election, so between Albuquerque's resignation on 5 February and the dissolution on 27 March nothing could be done, and a region governed by a resigned cabinet waited seven weeks for a clock to run out. The edge argues that constraint, which is why it is `precondition-of`.
explanations.2024-madeiran-regional-election--2025-ma: The ballot of May 2024 returned the same party, the same leader and the same absence of a majority as the one eight months before it, in an assembly where the opposition had by then decided it would not tolerate him. The motion of censure approved in December is what the result made available and what the parties used; the dissolution and the election of 23 March 2025 followed within three months. An election that changes nothing in a chamber that has stopped supporting the government is a cause of the next election, and that is what this edge says.
explanations.bpn-nationalisation-2008--troika-bailout: The rescue put a large and, for years, uncertain liability onto the public accounts at the moment when the market was pricing Portuguese debt on exactly such uncertainties. It is one of the specific reasons the numbers looked worse in 2011 than they had in 2008.
explanations.costa-resigns-2023--legislative-election: The resignation left a majority government without the prime minister it had been built around, and the president chose dissolution over a replacement from the same benches. The election of March 2024 is the direct consequence of that choice, and its date was set within a week of the resignation.
explanations.covid-19-pandemic--covid-19-pandemic-in-: The European epidemic is the same epidemic: the first confirmed cases on the continent, in France on 24 January 2020, were travellers from Wuhan, and the northern Italian cluster of February is what turned importation into transmission across the continent. The atlas keeps the two as separate events because the Portuguese chain runs through the European one and not through the Chinese one — what closed Portugal in March 2020 was an epidemic already inside Europe and inside Spain.
explanations.covid-19-pandemic-in-europe--covid-state: Portugal confirmed its first cases on 2 March 2020, closed the schools on the 16th and had a state of emergency declared on the 18th — the first under the constitution of 1976 — with the epidemic in Spain a fortnight ahead of its own and Italy's hospitals already overwhelmed. The decision was taken on what was happening in Europe rather than on what had yet happened here: the Portuguese curve at the moment of the declaration was small, and the argument made for the measures was explicitly that Italy and Spain showed what the following fortnight would look like.
explanations.covid-state-of-emergency-2020--marcelo-r: The presidential election of January 2021 was held in the worst weeks of the winter wave, under the restrictions the emergency had normalised, with campaigning curtailed and turnout below forty per cent. A first-round win against a divided field owed something to a contest nobody was able to fight in the ordinary way.
explanations.covid-state-of-emergency-2020--world-you: Lisbon had been given the celebration for 2022. The pandemic that the state of emergency marks in Portugal is why it was held in August 2023 instead, and why it was planned twice. The edge is about the postponement and about nothing else.
explanations.crisis-portugal--2011-portuguese-legisla: The ballot of 5 June 2011 was early and it was about the crisis: the fourth austerity package was voted down in March, José Sócrates resigned, and the country voted six weeks after the request for assistance, under a memorandum the two largest opposition parties had already signed. Probable rather than settled because an early election always has more than one proximate cause — the arithmetic of the minority government returned in 2009 is the other, and the atlas already draws that line to the bailout rather than here.
explanations.crisis-portugal--troika-bailout-2011--ca: The request of 6 April 2011 is what the crisis produced. By the spring of 2011 the state could not repay or refinance its debt on the market at a rate the treasury could carry; parliament had rejected the fourth austerity package, the government had resigned, and the memorandum with the Commission, the European Central Bank and the Fund was signed six weeks later. The direction is not in question and the record at the other end says the same thing from its own side. What is argued about is the composition of the crisis rather than this link, and the atlas puts that argument on the edge from the euro.
explanations.euromaidan--russo-ukrainian-war--caused: The soldiers without insignia appeared in Crimea on 27 February 2014, five days after Yanukovych left Kyiv, and the sequence is not in doubt: Russia acted when the government it had just spent a winter defending fell, and its stated justification was that what had happened in Kyiv was a coup against a legitimate president and a threat to Russian speakers. The claim is about the occasion and the justification. Whether the annexation was an improvisation or the execution of a plan the crisis merely brought forward is argued, and this edge does not settle it.
explanations.full-scale-russo-ukrainian-war--bucha-ma: Bucha was occupied because it lies on the road from Belarus to Kyiv, which is the axis of the attempt to take the capital in the first days of the invasion, and the killings were done during that occupation and found when the column withdrew at the end of March. The claim is about the occasion and nothing more: what a Russian army was doing in a commuter town thirty kilometres from Kyiv is answered entirely by the plan of 24 February. Whether the killings were ordered, tolerated or done by units out of control is a question of command responsibility that this edge does not decide.
explanations.full-scale-russo-ukrainian-war--wagner-g: The mutiny of June 2023 came out of a quarrel about the conduct of one war: Wagner had been given the assault on Bakhmut, had recruited tens of thousands of convicts to do it, and Prigozhin spent the spring accusing the Ministry of Defence of starving his men of ammunition. The order to bring private companies under ministry contracts, which would have ended Wagner as a separate army, is what he moved against. Without the war there is no force of that size under a private command and no quarrel over its supply.
explanations.gaza-war--gaza-genocide--caused: The two records describe the same eighteen months from different positions: one is the war, the other is the finding that the way it has been fought amounts to the destruction of a people as such. The edge exists because the atlas holds both and a reader is owed the relation between them; it is marked disputed because that relation is the thing in dispute, and this project's worst available mistake would be to present either side of it as settled. What is not in dispute and is not the subject of this edge: the scale of the killing, the destruction of the housing, hospitals and universities of the Strip, and the displacement of nearly its whole population.
explanations.gaza-war--twelve-day-war--precondition-o: The war of June 2025 is the last step of a regional escalation that began on 8 October 2023, when Hezbollah opened the northern front, and ran through the Houthi campaign in the Red Sea, the killing of Iranian officers in Damascus, and the two direct exchanges of missiles between Iran and Israel in April and October 2024 — the first in the history of either state. By 2025 Iran's allies had been broken and its air defences opened, which is the condition of a surprise attack on the nuclear sites. The immediate cause was the nuclear programme and the negotiation that had stalled over it; what the Gaza war supplied was the sequence that made a direct war between the two states ordinary.
explanations.geringonca-2015--legislative-election-20: The PS returned in 2019 with more votes than in 2015, and the four years of the arrangement are the usual explanation: incomes recovered, the government held its term, and the parties that had supported it did not bring it down before the end.

The election of January 2022 was called because the arrangement of 2015 had ended: the two parties that had kept the PS in office voted its budget down, and the president dissolved parliament rather than let a government continue without one. The arrangement is therefore a precondition of the election in the strict sense — the election happened at that moment because the arrangement had existed and had stopped.
explanations.geringonca-2015--marcelo-elected-preside: The presidential campaign ran through the new government's first weeks, and the winner made cohabitation with it the substance of his candidacy rather than an afterthought, which is what allowed a candidate of the defeated side to win in the first round. A different government in November would have produced a different January.
explanations.government-falls-2025--legislative-elect: A government defeated on a motion of confidence resigns, and with no alternative majority available in the same chamber the president dissolved parliament rather than look for one. The poll of 18 May follows from the vote of 11 March with nothing between them but the campaign.
explanations.legislative-election-2015--geringonca-20: The election produced a chamber in which the largest list had no majority and the parties to its left had one between them. That arithmetic, and not any prior intention — the PS had campaigned against exactly such an arrangement — is what made a minority government supported from outside by the Bloco de Esquerda and the PCP possible for the first time since 1974.
explanations.legislative-election-2019--legislative-e: The government elected in 2019 governed without renewing the written agreements of 2015 and fell when the budget for 2022 was rejected by the same parties it had stopped writing agreements with. The second election follows from the terms on which the first government was formed rather than from any single vote.
explanations.legislative-election-2022--2022-portugue: Rio had led the party into two legislative elections and lost both, the second to the first absolute majority any party had won since 2005, and he did not stand again. The leadership ballot of 28 May follows from that defeat as directly as the Socialist ballot of July 2011 followed from theirs: the contest existed because the leader who had just lost would not be the leader at the next election.
explanations.legislative-election-2022--costa-resigns: An absolute majority meant that the prime minister could not be forced out by any vote in the chamber, so his going could only be his own act; it also meant that when he went, the majority was left without the person it had been assembled around. Both halves of that follow from the result of January 2022 rather than from the inquiry.
explanations.legislative-election-2022--legislative-e: The majority elected in January 2022 did not last two years, and the election of March 2024 is where its collapse was settled: the same electorate, two years later, returned a chamber in which the PS was no longer the largest list and a party founded in 2019 held fifty seats.
explanations.legislative-election-2024--montenegro-go: The Aliança Democrática was the largest list and the only formation able to govern without Chega, whose support the winner had refused during the campaign and refused again after it. The minority government appointed on 2 April is what that refusal and that arithmetic left available.
explanations.montenegro-government-2024--government-f: A minority government that had ruled out the only party able to give it a majority had no way of answering questions about the prime minister's family company except by asking the chamber to confirm it. The chamber did not, and the motion the government lost was its own: the fall follows from the terms on which it had taken office eleven months earlier.
explanations.orange-revolution--euromaidan--precondit: Euromaidan is the same square, over the same question of which way the country faces, against the same politician. What 2004 established was the repertoire — the permanent occupation of Independence Square as the way a Ukrainian government is challenged — and what it failed to establish is the reason the repertoire was needed again: the constitutional and anti-corruption settlement of 2005 did not hold, and Yanukovych returned to the presidency by election in 2010. The claim is about the precedent and the unfinished business, not that 2004 caused 2013, whose trigger was the association agreement and Russian pressure against it.
explanations.pedrogao-grande-fires-2017--october-fire: The failures the Independent Technical Commission found in June — the alert, the closing of the roads, the emergency communications network — had not been repaired by 15 October, and the second wave met the same system with the same gaps. This is a claim about what was not done in the four months between them, not that one fire lit the other.
explanations.russo-georgian-war--russo-ukrainian-war-: What happened in Georgia in 2008 was done again in Ukraine in 2014 in the same order: a separatist territory supported and then garrisoned, a passportisation of its residents that supplied a protection claim, a rapid operation the West was not prepared for, and a recognition of the result that nobody was going to reverse. The four months of Western sanction that followed 2008 lapsed and the reset with Moscow was under way within a year. The claim is that the precedent and its cost were both established in 2008; the causes of 2014 are in Ukraine, and this edge does not reach for them.
explanations.russo-ukrainian-war--full-scale-russo-uk: The invasion of February 2022 is not the beginning of a war but a decision to end by force what eight years of the existing one had failed to settle. The Minsk agreements had committed Ukraine to a constitutional status for the occupied districts that no Ukrainian parliament would pass and Russia to a withdrawal it never made, so the front line froze and the political instrument for changing it was exhausted; Moscow recognised the two republics as states on 21 February 2022 and invaded three days later. The claim is that the earlier war supplied the stalemate, the pretext and the recognised entities the invasion was launched to protect.
explanations.troika-bailout-2011--bes-resolution-2014: The resolution was carried out under the supervisory regime the 2011 programme had imposed and paid for out of the bank solvency support line the programme had provided. Without that money and that framework the Banco de Portugal would have had to choose between a rescue it could not fund and a disorderly failure; whether the same programme also delayed the recognition of the group's losses is a separate argument this edge does not make.
explanations.troika-bailout-2011--troika-programme-en: The programme signed in May 2011 was written to run for three years, and the exit of May 2014 is that term reached rather than a separate decision. What was decided was the manner of it: the government left without the precautionary line the lenders had prepared, and the IMF's own evaluation records that choice as contested at the time.
explanations.troika-programme-ends-2014--legislative-: The coalition went to the polls seventeen months after the exit and made it the case for its own continuation, so the campaign was fought on whether the adjustment had worked. The result — the most votes and no majority — is the answer the electorate gave to that case, and it is why the arithmetic of the chamber, rather than the size of the largest list, decided what came next.
